transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

I... well, they told me I needed to come in. It's just... things at work. 

I keep hearing these... voices. Coming from the call-light speakers, mostly. And the vents in the hallway. They keep telling me which patient records have been changed. It's... it's as clear as somebody standing right next to me. Even when the unit is dead quiet and... well, nobody else seems to hear it. So, I'm here.
Do you hear these voices even when you're not at work or in similar environments?
No. Just... like I said, it's the call-lights. And the vents on the unit. That's where they are.
Do the voices say anything about you or your actions, or do they make you believe something that others might not agree with?

Well... they mostly just talk about the charts. The wound-care charts. I... I know they're showing a pattern. Management doesn't want anyone to see it. 

My supervisor, she... she says it's just late entries. Or coding mistakes. But I know better. I know they're watching what I write in the system. Because... well, I'm the one who caught it.
Do you feel that people outside of work, like friends or family, might also be involved in watching or monitoring you?
No. Just... no. It's only at the facility. My family doesn't... they don't have anything to do with the charts.
Do you believe that the voices you hear are part of a plan to watch or control you in some way?

I already told you about the charts. The wound-care charts. It's... it's a pattern, and management doesn't want it out. My supervisor keeps making excuses, saying it's just coding mistakes, but... I know they're watching what I put in the system. Because I saw it. I caught it. So... yes. They're watching me.
Have you ever believed something to be true that others around you did not agree with or thought was unusual, outside of this situation at work?
No. Just... just the charts. I don't... I don't know what else you mean. It's just what's happening at the facility.
Have you ever had thoughts that something was happening that others didn’t believe, even when you weren’t at work or dealing with patient charts?
I... I thought I just said that. No. I don't... I don't know why you keep asking about other things. It's just what's happening at work. That's it.
Do you ever have beliefs or suspicions that others don’t share when you’re not at work, such as about things unrelated to patient charts or the facility?
I don't... I don't understand why we keep going over this. I just told you. No. It's just the charts. Nothing else.

latest_inference.note: The patient's delusional beliefs appear to be restricted to a single theme (patient charts and workplace surveillance) without evidence of other delusional themes or broader psychotic features. This supports a diagnosis of Delusional Disorder, Somatic Type (F22.0). Other unspecified and other specified schizophrenia spectrum disorders (F22.8, F22.9) are less likely given the monothematic delusion and lack of additional psychotic symptoms.
